newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast products steady to slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast products steady to slightly higher.

text.p: LOS ANGELES, Jan 3 (Reuter) U.S. West Coast spot refined products prices were steady to slightly higher Friday, as trade thinned ahead of the weekend, dealers said.
Traders and company officials said Pacific Northwest refiners operated normally following severe storms last weekend, which shut at least one plant.
"We are in normal operations," said a spokesman for Texaco's 136,000 barrel-per-day refinery in Anacortes, Wash., refinery.
Industry sources said Tosco's plant in Ferndale, Wash., shut for about a day earlier this week.
The API said West Coast refineries for the week ended Dec. 27 were operated at 89.7 percent of capacity, down 0.5 percentage points from the prior week.

Gasoline inventories on hand at PADD V West Coast refineries were down 1.01 million barrels compared to the prior week, but remained 1.65 million barrels above the same week last year, the trade group said.
Los Angeles jet fuel prices rose a notional four cents to 87/89 cents a gallon, due to a squeeze in prompt supplies.
